newsitem.title: MEXICO: Four die in clash between Mexican army, rebels.
newsitem.headline: Four die in clash between Mexican army, rebels.

text.p: Four people were killed and three wounded on Saturday in a clash between Mexican troops and rebels in a mountainous area of the southwestern state of Guerrero, the government said.
A Defense Ministry statement said the clash came at 3 p.m. local time (2000 GMT) when army troops were ambushed by rebels from the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) near the town of Tepozonalco.
The statement said two army sergeants and two civilians wearing EPR uniforms died in the clash, which took place about 62 miles (100 km) east of the state capital Chilpancingo.
Three army doctors were also wounded in the ambush, which the statement said came as the army patrol returned from helping victims of a heavy hailstorm in the region.
The EPR sprang up in Guerrero at the end of June last year calling for a Marxist popular uprising to overthrow President Ernesto Zedillo's government.

After a series of attacks at the end of August and sporadic shootings in ensuing months, the group had lapsed into relative inactivity this year, saying it would concentrate on "armed propaganda" instead. But a few weeks ago, EPR leaders warned reporters armed conflict was "imminent" because of what they termed continuing hostilities by the government.
